claim: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have been limited to a few mammalian species.
source: However, they have been limited to a few mammalian species.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background information without specific data or citations in this sentence.

claim: A set of four mammalian transcription factor genes used to generate iPSCs in mouse and humans can induce a partially reprogrammed pluripotent stem cell (PRPSCs) state in vertebrate and invertebrate model organisms.
source: Here we found that a set of four mammalian transcription factor genes used to generate iPSCs in mouse and humans can induce a partially reprogrammed pluripotent stem cell (PRPSCs) state in vertebrate and invertebrate model organisms, in mammals, birds, fish, and fly, which span 550 million years from a common ancestor.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The mammalian transcription factors can induce PRPSCs in mammals, birds, fish, and fly, which span 550 million years from a common ancestor.
source: Here we found that a set of four mammalian transcription factor genes used to generate iPSCs in mouse and humans can induce a partially reprogrammed pluripotent stem cell (PRPSCs) state in vertebrate and invertebrate model organisms, in mammals, birds, fish, and fly, which span 550 million years from a common ancestor.
evidence: The phylogenetic span is stated and supported by citation to Sullivan et al., 2006 elsewhere in the text, and experimental data is provided for each species.

claim: These findings are one of the first to show cross-lineage stem cell-like induction.
source: These findings are one of the first to show cross-lineage stem cell-like induction, and to generate pluripotent-like cells for several of these species with in vivo chimeras.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings, based on the authors' knowledge of the field.

claim: The study generated pluripotent-like cells for several species with in vivo chimeras.
source: These findings are one of the first to show cross-lineage stem cell-like induction, and to generate pluripotent-like cells for several of these species with in vivo chimeras.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing chimera formation in chicken and zebrafish.

claim: The stem-cell state may be highly conserved across a wide phylogenetic range.
source: We suggest that the stem-cell state may be highly conserved across a wide phylogenetic range.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Stem cells are in an early undifferentiated state and have the potential to differentiate into a variety of cell types and tissues.
source: Stem cells are in an early undifferentiated state and have the potential to differentiate into a variety of cell types and tissues, both in vitro and in vivo, including in developing embryos and grafted adult tissues (Badylak et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Stem cells provide a powerful platform to study development.
source: Accordingly, stem cells provide a powerful platform to study development (Arendt, 2008), tissue regeneration (Langer and Vacanti, 1999; Rosselló et al., 2009), disease mechanisms (Colman and Dreesen, 2009), and gene therapeutic approaches to the brain and other organs (Hwang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Arendt, 2008.

claim: Stem cells provide a powerful platform to study tissue regeneration.
source: Accordingly, stem cells provide a powerful platform to study development (Arendt, 2008), tissue regeneration (Langer and Vacanti, 1999; Rosselló et al., 2009), disease mechanisms (Colman and Dreesen, 2009), and gene therapeutic approaches to the brain and other organs (Hwang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Langer and Vacanti, 1999; Rosselló et al., 2009.

claim: Stem cells provide a powerful platform to study disease mechanisms.
source: Accordingly, stem cells provide a powerful platform to study development (Arendt, 2008), tissue regeneration (Langer and Vacanti, 1999; Rosselló et al., 2009), disease mechanisms (Colman and Dreesen, 2009), and gene therapeutic approaches to the brain and other organs (Hwang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Colman and Dreesen, 2009.

claim: Stem cells provide a powerful platform to study gene therapeutic approaches to the brain and other organs.
source: Accordingly, stem cells provide a powerful platform to study development (Arendt, 2008), tissue regeneration (Langer and Vacanti, 1999; Rosselló et al., 2009), disease mechanisms (Colman and Dreesen, 2009), and gene therapeutic approaches to the brain and other organs (Hwang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hwang et al., 2011.

claim: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) have the potential to be differentiated to most if not all cell types (pluripotent).
source: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) have the potential to be differentiated to most if not all cell types (pluripotent), whereas more differentiated stem cells, such as those in the skin, have a more restricted differentiation potential (multipotent or unipotent) (Collas et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Collas et al., 2007.

claim: More differentiated stem cells, such as those in the skin, have a more restricted differentiation potential (multipotent or unipotent).
source: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) have the potential to be differentiated to most if not all cell types (pluripotent), whereas more differentiated stem cells, such as those in the skin, have a more restricted differentiation potential (multipotent or unipotent) (Collas et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Collas et al., 2007.

claim: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are once mature cells that have been de-differentiated to become like the embryonic state.
source: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are once mature cells that have been de-differentiated to become like the embryonic state (Thomson et al., 1998; Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006; Takahashi et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2007; Maherali and Hochedlinger, 2008; Stadtfeld et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: iPSCs can be made from differentiated cells, such as skin or fibroblasts, of an individual and do not require isolating cells from 2–6 day old embryos.
source: One major advantage of iPSCs is that they can be made from differentiated cells, such as skin or fibroblasts, of an individual and do not require isolating cells from 2–6 day old embryos, which is controversial for human studies (Lo and Parham, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about iPSCs, with citation supporting the controversy aspect.

claim: Simple over-expression of four genes (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-myc) was sufficient to generate iPSCs from adult cells of mice.
source: The finding that simple over-expression of four genes (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-myc) was sufficient to generate iPSCs from adult cells of mice (Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006) and humans (Takahashi et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2007; Sommer et al., 2009) made the process of generating and studying stem cells much more tractable in certain other mammalian species, where it was once difficult to generate stem cells, such as in rats (Li and Ding, 2010) and pigs (Wu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006.

claim: Simple over-expression of four genes (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-myc) was sufficient to generate iPSCs from adult cells of humans.
source: The finding that simple over-expression of four genes (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-myc) was sufficient to generate iPSCs from adult cells of mice (Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006) and humans (Takahashi et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2007; Sommer et al., 2009) made the process of generating and studying stem cells much more tractable in certain other mammalian species, where it was once difficult to generate stem cells, such as in rats (Li and Ding, 2010) and pigs (Wu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Takahashi et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2007; Sommer et al., 2009.

claim: The four-gene approach made the process of generating and studying stem cells much more tractable in certain other mammalian species, such as in rats and pigs.
source: The finding that simple over-expression of four genes (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-myc) was sufficient to generate iPSCs from adult cells of mice (Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006) and humans (Takahashi et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2007; Sommer et al., 2009) made the process of generating and studying stem cells much more tractable in certain other mammalian species, where it was once difficult to generate stem cells, such as in rats (Li and Ding, 2010) and pigs (Wu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li and Ding, 2010 for rats and Wu et al., 2009 for pigs.

claim: Important issues in biology are addressed in experimental systems other than mammals, specifically in birds, fish, and flies.
source: However, important issues in biology are addressed in experimental systems other than mammals, specifically in birds (Jarvis, 2004, 2007; Jarvis et al., 2005), fish (Fetcho et al., 2008), and flies (Kuo et al., 2006; Yu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations for each organism type.

claim: Some animals have traits similar to humans that are not found in closely related non-human primates or commonly used laboratory animals, including vocal learning in parrots and songbirds.
source: Some of these animals have traits similar to humans that are not found in closely related non-human primates or commonly used laboratory animals. These include vocal learning in parrots and songbirds (Jarvis, 2004), widespread adult neurogenesis in non-mammalian vertebrates (Nottebohm, 2002; Kaslin et al., 2008), and vascularization and organ regeneration in zebrafish (Poss et al., 2002; Stoletov and Klemke, 2008; Yaqoob and Schwerte, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jarvis, 2004.

claim: Widespread adult neurogenesis occurs in non-mammalian vertebrates.
source: Some of these animals have traits similar to humans that are not found in closely related non-human primates or commonly used laboratory animals. These include vocal learning in parrots and songbirds (Jarvis, 2004), widespread adult neurogenesis in non-mammalian vertebrates (Nottebohm, 2002; Kaslin et al., 2008), and vascularization and organ regeneration in zebrafish (Poss et al., 2002; Stoletov and Klemke, 2008; Yaqoob and Schwerte, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nottebohm, 2002; Kaslin et al., 2008.

claim: Zebrafish exhibit vascularization and organ regeneration.
source: Some of these animals have traits similar to humans that are not found in closely related non-human primates or commonly used laboratory animals. These include vocal learning in parrots and songbirds (Jarvis, 2004), widespread adult neurogenesis in non-mammalian vertebrates (Nottebohm, 2002; Kaslin et al., 2008), and vascularization and organ regeneration in zebrafish (Poss et al., 2002; Stoletov and Klemke, 2008; Yaqoob and Schwerte, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Poss et al., 2002; Stoletov and Klemke, 2008; Yaqoob and Schwerte, 2010.

claim: Drosophila melanogaster is an attractive genetic model due to the short life span, large number of offspring, and applicability of many genetic techniques.
source: The arthropod Drosophila melanogaster is an attractive genetic model due to the short life span, large number of offspring, and applicability of many genetic techniques (van Ham et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to van Ham et al., 2009.

claim: Drosophila have been used to model Parkinson's, Huntington's, and Prion disease.
source: Drosophila have been used to model Parkinson's, Huntington's, and Prion disease.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge without specific citation in this sentence.

claim: Production of non-mammalian stem cells has been limited, due to problematic or unknown isolation procedures, and insufficient maintenance methods.
source: Unfortunately, production of non-mammalian stem cells has been limited, due to problematic or unknown isolation procedures, and insufficient maintenance methods (Lavial and Pain, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lavial and Pain, 2010.

claim: The study attempted to generate an iPSC state for non-mammalian vertebrate and invertebrate model species spanning over 550 million years from a common ancestor: in birds (galliformes and songbirds), fish (zebrafish), and insect (Drosophila).
source: Here we attempted to generate an iPSC state for non-mammalian vertebrate and invertebrate model species spanning over 550 million years from a common ancestor (Figure 1A) (Sullivan et al., 2006): in birds (galliformes and songbirds), fish (zebrafish), and insect (Drosophila).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach, with phylogenetic relationship supported by citation to Sullivan et al., 2006 and Figure 1A.

claim: The four transcription factor genes used to induce mammalian stem cells can produce a partial iPSC state that varies with degree of relationship to mammals.
source: We found that the four transcription factor genes used to induce mammalian stem cells can produce a partial iPSC state that varies with degree of relationship to mammals.
evidence: This is a main finding supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The mammalian (mouse) homolog of these genes induced this partial iPSC reprogrammed state in the non-mammalian cells of all species tested.
source: Moreover, the mammalian (mouse) homolog of these genes induced this partial iPSC reprogrammed state in the non-mammalian cells of all species tested, including inducing the ability of the vertebrate cells to incorporate into embryonic chimeras.
evidence: This is a main finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The mammalian genes induced the ability of the vertebrate cells to incorporate into embryonic chimeras.
source: Moreover, the mammalian (mouse) homolog of these genes induced this partial iPSC reprogrammed state in the non-mammalian cells of all species tested, including inducing the ability of the vertebrate cells to incorporate into embryonic chimeras.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing chimera formation.

claim: These findings are the first to generate iPSC-like cells across multiple non-mammalian species, using mammalian genes, in animal models where stem cells have been difficult or impossible to isolate.
source: These findings are the first that we are aware of to generate iPSC-like cells across multiple non-mammalian species, using mammalian genes, in animal models where stem cells have been difficult or impossible to isolate (Zwaka, 2008; Lavial and Pain, 2010).
evidence: This is a claim about novelty, supported by citations indicating previous difficulties.

claim: The mouse genes might work in birds despite the separation of ∼300 million years ago from a common ancestor with mammals because the overall conservation between birds and mammals was good (80–98% overall amino acid identity).
source: We surmised that the mouse genes might work in birds despite the separation of ∼300 million years ago (MYA) from a common ancestor with mammals (Figure 1A), because although there were stretches of low homology and divergent sequences in three of the four genes (Oct4, Klf4, and c-myc), the overall conservation between birds and mammals was good (80–98% overall amino acid identity; Figure 1B–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a rationale based on sequence analysis data shown in figures.

claim: All four genes had highly conserved DNA binding domains.
source: Furthermore, all four genes had highly conserved DNA binding domains (Figure 1—figure supplement 2; red boxes).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The transformed avian cells showed a number of stem cell features absent from control fibroblasts and present in mouse ESC and iPSC controls, and chicken ESC controls.
source: The transformed avian cells showed a number of stem cell features absent from control fibroblasts and present in our mouse ESC and iPSC controls, and chicken ESC controls.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in subsequent sentences and figures.

claim: Within 5 days, avian cells transformed from fibroblast morphology to colonies with characteristic clustered stem cell-like morphology.
source: This included, within 5 days, transformation from fibroblast morphology (Figure 2A) to colonies with characteristic clustered stem cell-like morphology (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by images in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: The transformed avian colonies had strong alkaline phosphatase (ALP) enzyme activity, whereas the starting fibroblasts did not.
source: These colonies had strong alkaline phosphatase (ALP) enzyme activity (Figure 2D), a characteristic of early and mature stem and tumor cells (O'Connor et al., 2008), whereas the starting fibroblasts did not (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and 2D, with citation for ALP as a stem cell marker.

claim: The transformed avian cells expressed Stem Cell Specific Antigen-1 (SSEA-1), while none was detected in control fibroblasts.
source: They expressed Stem Cell Specific Antigen-1 (SSEA-1; Figure 2F), while none was detected in control fibroblasts (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: An average of 20% of the wells had iPSC-like cells, as measured by colony morphology and ALP activity.
source: An average of 20% of the wells had iPSC-like cells, as measured by colony morphology and ALP activity (measured from seven independent experiments for each avian species).
evidence: This is quantitative data from experiments.

claim: Later iterations with different media conditions produced transformed cells in up to 90% of the wells.
source: Later iterations with different media conditions produced transformed cells in up to 90% of the wells (Dai et al., unpublished date).
evidence: This is data from unpublished work by the authors.

claim: The higher the viral titer used, the more colonies were produced.
source: The higher the viral titer used, the more colonies were produced (Figure 2—figure supplement 1); the highest titer, 109 U/ml, was used in the above experiments.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mouse colonies as well as the individual cells within the colonies appeared on average slightly larger than avian cells, while avian cells appeared more clustered.
source: We noticed some differences between the mouse and avian colonies, in that the mouse colonies as well as the individual cells within the colonies appeared on average slightly larger, while avian cells appeared more clustered.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Similar differences have been observed when comparing human and mouse colonies.
source: Similar differences have been observed when comparing human and mouse colonies (Nichols and Smith, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nichols and Smith, 2009.

claim: The mouse and avian iPSC-like colonies were similar to those in established lines of mouse and chicken ESCs that were treated under the same growth conditions.
source: The mouse and avian iPSC-like colonies were similar to those in established lines of mouse and chicken ESCs that we treated under the same growth conditions, including differences between the species (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: This is supported by comparison data shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: The transformed avian cells expressed the four exogenous mammalian genes.
source: Like our mouse control iPSCs, the transformed avian cells (chicken, quail, and finch) expressed the four exogenous mammalian genes (Figure 3A–D; as determined by quantitative RT-PCR with mouse specific probes; Supplementary file 1C).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: After the first and second passages, three of the endogenous avian homologs (Oct4, Sox2, c-myc) were significantly upregulated 10–100-fold in the presence of their mammalian counterparts (except c-myc in quail).
source: After the first and second passages (3–4 weeks), three of the endogenous avian homologs (Oct4, Sox2, c-myc) were significantly upregulated 10–100-fold in the presence of their mammalian counterparts (except c-myc in quail; Figure 3A–D; green).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: The levels of induction of the endogenous and exogenous expression of Oct4, Sox2, and c-myc in chicken and mouse cells were similar to the control chicken and mouse ES cell.
source: The levels of induction of the endogenous and exogenous expression of these three genes in our chicken and mouse cells were similar to the control chicken and mouse ES cell.
evidence: This is based on comparison of qRT-PCR data.

claim: The level of induction in quail and zebra finch was lower (4–40-fold), but still statistically significant (p<0.0001, ANOVA) with no overlap in the expression detected in five replication experiments relative to the embryonic fibroblast controls.
source: The level of induction in quail and zebra finch was lower (4–40-fold), but still statistically significant (p<0.0001, ANOVA) with no overlap in the expression detected in five replication experiments relative to the embryonic fibroblast controls.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of qRT-PCR data.

claim: Klf4 was upregulated in mouse control iPSC and ESC, but not upregulated in any of the avian species.
source: The fourth gene, Klf4, was upregulated in our mouse control iPSC and ESC, but not upregulated in any of the avian species (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Klf4 was not upregulated in the established control chicken ESC line, relative to the chicken embryonic fibroblast.
source: However, Klf4 was also not upregulated in the established control chicken ESC line (Figure 3C–D), relative to the chicken embryonic fibroblast.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: All avian species showed significant induced expression of two other endogenous stem cell markers, nanog and vasa, not present in the STEMMCA vector.
source: All avian species also showed significant induced expression of two other endogenous stem cell markers, nanog and vasa, not present in the STEMMCA vector, with levels more similar among species but lower than the mouse (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E-G.

claim: After about the fifth passage, the exogenous mouse genes were either completely (mouse and chicken) or partially (quail and finch) silenced.
source: After about the fifth passage (2–3 months), the exogenous mouse genes were either completely (mouse and chicken) or partially (quail and finch) silenced, and this was associated with a concomitant further increase in some of the endogenous species-specific homologs (Figure 3G–J; including c-myc in quail as well as vasa and nanog, Figure 3K–L).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3G-L.

claim: Exogenous gene silencing was associated with a concomitant further increase in some of the endogenous species-specific homologs.
source: After about the fifth passage (2–3 months), the exogenous mouse genes were either completely (mouse and chicken) or partially (quail and finch) silenced, and this was associated with a concomitant further increase in some of the endogenous species-specific homologs (Figure 3G–J; including c-myc in quail as well as vasa and nanog, Figure 3K–L).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3G-L.

claim: Klf4 was still very low relative to the starting fibroblast controls in the avian cells after the fifth passage, except for a small increase in some of the finch cell lines.
source: However, Klf4 was still very low relative to the starting fibroblast controls in the avian cells, except for a small increase in some of the finch cell lines (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: The transformed zebrafish cells showed cell colony formation, ALP activity, and expression of SSEA1 protein.
source: We found similar results for transformed zebrafish cells as for bird putative iPSC and ESC. This included cell colony formation (Figure 2B), ALP activity (Figure 2D), and expression of SSEA1 protein (Figure 2E), initial high expression (Figure 3A–D) and then silencing of the exogenous mouse genes by the fifth passage (Figure 3G–J), and absence of induction of endogenous Klf4 (Figure 3D–J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Transformed zebrafish cells showed initial high expression and then silencing of the exogenous mouse genes by the fifth passage.
source: We found similar results for transformed zebrafish cells as for bird putative iPSC and ESC. This included cell colony formation (Figure 2B), ALP activity (Figure 2D), and expression of SSEA1 protein (Figure 2E), initial high expression (Figure 3A–D) and then silencing of the exogenous mouse genes by the fifth passage (Figure 3G–J), and absence of induction of endogenous Klf4 (Figure 3D–J).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3A-D and 3G-J.

claim: Transformed zebrafish cells showed absence of induction of endogenous Klf4.
source: We found similar results for transformed zebrafish cells as for bird putative iPSC and ESC. This included cell colony formation (Figure 2B), ALP activity (Figure 2D), and expression of SSEA1 protein (Figure 2E), initial high expression (Figure 3A–D) and then silencing of the exogenous mouse genes by the fifth passage (Figure 3G–J), and absence of induction of endogenous Klf4 (Figure 3D–J).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3D-J.

claim: There was induction of the endogenous stem cell marker Vasa in zebrafish transformed cells.
source: There was also induction of the endogenous stem cell marker Vasa (Figure 3E–F; K–L).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E-F and K-L.

claim: The only significant difference between the zebrafish and birds was lack of Nanog induction in the fish cells.
source: The only significant difference between the zebrafish and birds was lack of Nanog induction in the fish cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The average zebrafish colony size was smaller than avian colonies.
source: The average zebrafish colony size was also smaller (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an observation from images in Figure 2B.

claim: The transformed Drosophila S2 cells showed colony formation, although the colonies were notably fewer, smaller in size, and even darker than the vertebrate colonies.
source: We found that the transformed Drosophila S2 cells with the STEMCCA lentivirus or plasmid containing the four factors showed colony formation, although the colonies were notably fewer, smaller in size, and even darker than the vertebrate colonies (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an observation from images in Figure 2B.

claim: The Drosophila colonies showed ALP activity.
source: The Drosophila colonies, like those of vertebrates, showed ALP activity (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The Drosophila transformed cells expressed the exogenous mouse genes.
source: They also expressed the exogenous mouse genes (Figure 3M) and, similar to the avian and fish transformed cells, the Drosophila transformed cells had induced expression of two of four endogenous homologues to the mammalian cassette, VVL (Oct4 homolog) and dMyc (c-myc), low induction of SoxN (Sox2), and no induction of Luna (putative Klf4; Figure 3M).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: The Drosophila transformed cells had induced expression of two of four endogenous homologues to the mammalian cassette, VVL (Oct4 homolog) and dMyc (c-myc).
source: They also expressed the exogenous mouse genes (Figure 3M) and, similar to the avian and fish transformed cells, the Drosophila transformed cells had induced expression of two of four endogenous homologues to the mammalian cassette, VVL (Oct4 homolog) and dMyc (c-myc), low induction of SoxN (Sox2), and no induction of Luna (putative Klf4; Figure 3M).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: The Drosophila transformed cells showed low induction of SoxN (Sox2).
source: They also expressed the exogenous mouse genes (Figure 3M) and, similar to the avian and fish transformed cells, the Drosophila transformed cells had induced expression of two of four endogenous homologues to the mammalian cassette, VVL (Oct4 homolog) and dMyc (c-myc), low induction of SoxN (Sox2), and no induction of Luna (putative Klf4; Figure 3M).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: The Drosophila transformed cells showed no induction of Luna (putative Klf4).
source: They also expressed the exogenous mouse genes (Figure 3M) and, similar to the avian and fish transformed cells, the Drosophila transformed cells had induced expression of two of four endogenous homologues to the mammalian cassette, VVL (Oct4 homolog) and dMyc (c-myc), low induction of SoxN (Sox2), and no induction of Luna (putative Klf4; Figure 3M).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: There was a significant upregulation of four of six other known endogenous Drosophila adult stem cell markers, Dichaete, Escargot, Snail, and Vasa.
source: There was also a significant upregulation of four of six other known endogenous Drosophila adult stem cell markers, Dichaete, Escargot, Snail, and Vasa (Figure 3N) (Wilson and Dearden, 2008; Palasz and Kaminski, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3N, with citations for these being stem cell markers.

claim: Proliferation levels of the mouse, avian, and fish transformed cells were above their respective fibroblast controls after the first to third passage.
source: Proliferation levels of the mouse, avian, and fish transformed cells (measured by an MTT metabolic assay) were above their respective fibroblast controls after the first to third passage, depending on species (Figure 3O, green vs blue).
evidence: This is supported by MTT assay data shown in Figure 3O.

claim: The MTT levels of transformed vertebrate cells approached that of the mouse and chicken ESC lines.
source: The MTT levels at this time approached that of the mouse and chicken ESC lines (in red).
evidence: This is based on MTT assay data shown in Figure 3O.

claim: Vertebrate cells with the GFP-vector alone treated under identical conditions showed a continuous decrease in MTT levels, which was clearly associated with senescence.
source: Vertebrate cells with the GFP-vector alone treated under identical conditions instead showed a continuous decrease in MTT levels (in blue), which was clearly associated with senescence.
evidence: This is based on MTT assay data and observation of senescence.

claim: Transformed S2 cells exhibited enhanced proliferation levels at all passages compared to control S2 cells.
source: However, transformed S2 cells exhibited enhanced proliferation levels at all passages (Figure 3O; we did not assess the BG2 cells with MTT).
evidence: This is supported by MTT assay data shown in Figure 3O.

claim: Telomerase activity was activated in all transformed vertebrate cells, and at levels comparable to those seen in the mouse and chicken ESC lines.
source: Telomerase activity was also activated in all transformed vertebrate cells, and at levels comparable to those seen in the mouse and chicken ESC lines (Figure 3P).
evidence: This is supported by telomerase activity assay data shown in Figure 3P.

claim: Telomerase activity is a characteristic feature of immortal cell lines.
source: Telomerase activity is a characteristic feature of immortal cell lines (Thomson et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Thomson et al., 1998.

claim: The transformed Drosophila cells did not have telomerase activity.
source: Unlike the vertebrate cells, however, the transformed Drosophila cells did not have telomerase activity (not shown), confirming known absence of telomerase in the Drosophila genome (Gomes et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on experimental data (not shown) and citation to Gomes et al., 2010.

claim: The chicken iPSC-like lines displayed a normal karyotype of macro chromosomes in the majority of the spreads analyzed (90%; 18 out of 20).
source: The chicken iPSC-like lines (Figure 4C, male shown) displayed a normal karyotype of macro chromosomes in the majority of the spreads analyzed (90%; 18 out of 20) compared to a standard (Nanda et al., 1999), control fibroblasts (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by karyotype data shown in Figure 4C-D, with citation to a standard.

claim: The majority of the zebra finch (female) iPSC-like lines (90%) displayed normal karyotype of macro chromosomes.
source: The majority of the zebra finch (female) iPSC-like lines (90%) also displayed normal karyotype of macro chromosomes (Figure 4E, female shown).
evidence: This is supported by karyotype data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The minority of cells that were not normal had tetraploid spreads, but in both iPSC-like and control cells.
source: The minority of cells that were not normal had tetraploid spreads, but in both iPSC-like and control cells: two out of 20 in the chicken iPSC-like cells and controls, two out of 20 in the finch iPSC-like cell, and one out of 20 in the finch control.
evidence: This is quantitative data from karyotype analysis.

claim: The tetraploid spreads were a result of a doubling of the chromosome complement, which is common in cultured cells.
source: This was a result of a doubling of the chromosome complement, which is common in cultured cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on established knowledge about cultured cells.

claim: Major chromosomal arrangements did not occur as a result of the transformation in avian cells.
source: These results with at least the avian cells suggest that major chromosomal arrangements did not occur as a result of the transformation.
evidence: This is an inference from the karyotype data.

claim: Formation of embryoid bodies (EBs) was achieved from the avian, fish, and Drosophila iPSC-like cells.
source: Formation of EBs was achieved from the avian, fish, and Drosophila iPSC-like cells, and they appeared similar to those formed from our chicken and mouse ESC lines, and control mouse iPSCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by images in Figure 4A.

claim: The embryoid bodies from iPSC-like cells appeared similar to those formed from chicken and mouse ESC lines, and control mouse iPSCs.
source: Formation of EBs was achieved from the avian, fish, and Drosophila iPSC-like cells, and they appeared similar to those formed from our chicken and mouse ESC lines, and control mouse iPSCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on comparison of images in Figure 4A.

claim: No EB formation occurred with the control cells of any of the species (fibroblast or S2).
source: No EB formation occurred with the control cells of any of the species (fibroblast or S2), indicating that EB formation was specific to the iPSC-like cells and established ESCs.
evidence: This is experimental data showing specificity of EB formation.

claim: Differentiation into the three germ cell lineages was supported by quantitative RT-PCR of lineage-enriched genes showing over-expression relative to the fibroblasts of Brachyury (mesoderm), Nestin (endoderm), and Gata-4 (ectoderm) in all vertebrate species.
source: Differentiation into the three germ cell lineages was supported by quantitative RT-PCR of lineage-enriched genes showing over-expression relative to the fibroblasts of Brachyury (mesoderm), Nestin (endoderm), and Gata-4 (ectoderm) in all vertebrate species (Figure 4B) (Leahy et al., 1999; Murakami et al., 2004; Hailesellasse Sene et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B, with citations for the lineage markers.

claim: The expression of Brachyury, Nestin, and Gata-4 was much lower in undifferentiated mouse, avian, or fish iPSC-like cells.
source: Conversely, the expression of these genes was much lower in our undifferentiated mouse, avian, or fish iPSC-like cells (i.e., the iPSC-like, green).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Two (out of nine) of the chicken iPSC-like cells injected mice developed teratomas.
source: After 35 days, two (out of nine) of the chicken iPSC-like and three (out of nine) quail iPSC-like cells injected mice developed teratomas.
evidence: This is quantitative data from teratoma formation experiments.

claim: Three (out of nine) quail iPSC-like cells injected mice developed teratomas.
source: After 35 days, two (out of nine) of the chicken iPSC-like and three (out of nine) quail iPSC-like cells injected mice developed teratomas.
evidence: This is quantitative data from teratoma formation experiments.

claim: The teratomas from chicken and quail iPSC-like cells exhibited organized formation of endoderm (such as neuronal rossetts), mesoderm (such as bone), and ectoderm (such as G.I Tract), demonstrating pluripotency in vivo.
source: These teratomas exhibited organized formation of endoderm (such as neuronal rossetts, Figure 5A,D), mesoderm (such as bone, Figure 5B,E), and ectoderm (such as G.I Tract, Figure 5C,F), demonstrating pluripotency in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 5A-F.

claim: None of the controls generated teratomas.
source: None of the controls generated teratomas (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5H-I.

claim: None of the zebra finch iPSC-like cells formed teratomas, suggestive of possible species differences for in vivo pluripotency.
source: So far, none of the zebra finch iPSC-like cells formed teratomas, suggestive of possible species differences for in vivo pluripotency.
evidence: This is experimental data with speculative interpretation.

claim: The rate of chimera formation was about 16% for the chicken (four out of 25 attempts).
source: The rate of chimera formation was about 16% for the chicken (four out of 25 attempts) and 10% for fish embryos (10 out of 103 attempts).
evidence: This is quantitative data from chimera formation experiments.

claim: The rate of chimera formation was 10% for fish embryos (10 out of 103 attempts).
source: The rate of chimera formation was about 16% for the chicken (four out of 25 attempts) and 10% for fish embryos (10 out of 103 attempts).
evidence: This is quantitative data from chimera formation experiments.

claim: Embryos injected with iPSC-like cells were subject to higher mortality than those injected with control fibroblasts.
source: Embryos injected with iPSC-like cells were subject to higher mortality than those injected with control fibroblasts.
evidence: This is observational data from chimera experiments.

claim: In chicken, about 50% of the embryos did not reach the 3rd day of incubation, compared to only 20% for control cells.
source: In chicken, about 50% of the embryos did not reach the 3rd day of incubation, compared to only 20% for control cells.
evidence: This is quantitative data on embryo survival.

claim: With zebrafish, about 60% of embryos injected with the iPSC-like cells did not survive, while the rate was negligible in control fibroblast injected embryos.
source: Similarly with zebrafish, about 60% of embryos injected with the iPSC-like cells did not survive, while the rate was negligible in control fibroblast injected embryos.
evidence: This is quantitative data on embryo survival.

claim: These results are consistent with lower survival rates observed in iPSC-injected mice.
source: These results are consistent with lower survival rates observed in iPSC-injected mice (Maherali and Hochedlinger, 2008), and could be due to multiple factors, such as the iPSC causing tumors and some other type of aberrant growth.
evidence: This is a comparison to published data with citation, and speculation about causes.

claim: After 1 day, some of the iPSC-like-GFP injected fish embryos produced a secondary axis.
source: Interestingly, after 1 day, some of the iPSC-like-GFP injected fish embryos produced a secondary axis (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C), suggesting a disruption in the developmental program.
evidence: This is observational data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C, with speculative interpretation.

claim: The starting fibroblast cells did not survive in the 72hpf fish embryos or the ED4 chicken, and thus did not generate fluorescently labeled older chimeras.
source: However, the starting fibroblast cells did not survive in the 72hpf fish embryos or the ED4 chicken, and thus did not generate fluorescently labeled older chimeras (Figure 6A,E).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 6A and E.

claim: In some animals (both chicken and fish), the iPSC-like cells incorporated in nearly all organs of the body.
source: In some animals (both chicken and fish), the cells incorporated in nearly all organs of the body (Figure 6C,G), but for the most part they incorporated sporadically (chicken iPSC-like cells incorporation, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6C, G, and figure supplement 3.

claim: In the chicken, the iPSC-like cells differentiated into many cell types, including into muscle, intestines, skin, and brain.
source: In the chicken, the iPSC-like cells differentiated into many cell types, including into muscle, intestines, skin, and brain, while in the fish, most of the incorporation was observed in the stomach and the head (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: In the fish, most of the incorporation was observed in the stomach and the head.
source: In the chicken, the iPSC-like cells differentiated into many cell types, including into muscle, intestines, skin, and brain, while in the fish, most of the incorporation was observed in the stomach and the head (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: These features are similar to those seen in the early mouse chimeras created with mouse iPSC cells and chicken chimeras created with chicken ESC cells.
source: These features are similar to those seen in the early mouse chimeras created with mouse iPSC cells (Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006) and chicken chimeras created with chicken ESC cells (Lavial et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a comparison to published data supported by citations.

claim: Most surviving embryos looked normal with no overt differences from animals treated under the same conditions without injected cells or injected with non-transduced fibroblast cells.
source: Like those studies, most of our surviving embryos looked normal with no overt differences from animals treated under the same conditions without injected cells or injected with non-transduced fibroblast cells.
evidence: This is observational data from the experiments.

claim: The non-mammalian vertebrate cells generated with mammalian genes are pluripotent for at least non-germline cells in a developing animal in vivo.
source: These findings demonstrate that the non-mammalian vertebrate cells we generated with mammalian genes are pluripotent for at least non-germline cells in a developing animal in vivo, and functionally behave like mouse and chicken ESC and iPSC in vivo up until the ages analyzed.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the chimera formation data.

claim: The non-mammalian vertebrate cells generated with mammalian genes functionally behave like mouse and chicken ESC and iPSC in vivo up until the ages analyzed.
source: These findings demonstrate that the non-mammalian vertebrate cells we generated with mammalian genes are pluripotent for at least non-germline cells in a developing animal in vivo, and functionally behave like mouse and chicken ESC and iPSC in vivo up until the ages analyzed.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of experimental data.

claim: At least partially reprogrammed iPSC can be generated in non-mammalian species.
source: Our results indicate that at least partially reprogrammed iPSC can be generated in non-mammalian species and that the mammalian genes are sufficient to do so in both non-mammalian vertebrates and invertebrates.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all experimental data.

claim: The mammalian genes are sufficient to generate partially reprogrammed iPSC in both non-mammalian vertebrates and invertebrates.
source: Our results indicate that at least partially reprogrammed iPSC can be generated in non-mammalian species and that the mammalian genes are sufficient to do so in both non-mammalian vertebrates and invertebrates.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all experimental data.

claim: Others have recently shown that for one bird species, the quail, some of these properties can be induced using the human genes.
source: While our study was under review, others (Lu et al., 2012) have recently shown that for one bird species, the quail, some of these properties can be induced using the human genes.
evidence: This is a citation to concurrent work by others.

claim: The four human transcription factors in all aves (chicken, quail, zebra finch) and zebrafish cells produced results similar to the ones obtained with the mouse factors.
source: We also had tested the four human transcription factors in all aves (chicken, quail, zebra finch) and zebrafish cells and found results similar to the ones obtained with the mouse factors ('Materials and methods' and data not shown).
evidence: This is experimental data mentioned but not shown in detail.

claim: Characteristics which the non-mammalian iPSC-like cells have in common with mouse iPSCs and ESCs are colony morphology, marker expression of induced genes, reactivation of some endogenous pluripotency genes, transgene-independent self-renewal, embryoid body formation, teratoma generation (for chicken and quail), and the ability to contribute to different cell lineages in chimeric embryos (for chicken and zebrafish).
source: Characteristics which the non-mammalian iPSC-like cells we generated have in common with mouse iPSCs and ESCs are colony morphology, marker expression of induced genes, reactivation of some endogenous pluripotency genes, transgene-independent self-renewal, embryoid body formation, teratoma generation (for chicken and quail), and the ability to contribute to different cell lineages in chimeric embryos (for chicken and zebrafish; Table 1).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings, with reference to Table 1.

claim: These findings suggest that the induction process is relatively conserved.
source: These findings suggest that the induction process is relatively conserved.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data.

claim: Some differences to mouse iPSC cells include lack or little induction of Klf4.
source: Some differences to mouse iPSC cells include lack or little induction of Klf4, overall initial slower growth of cells, lower overall fold-expression increase in endogenous stem cell genes, and presence of autologously derived fibroblast cells for some of the avian species in the middle passages (Dai et al., unpublished date); the latter two traits are similar to some human ES cells (Draper et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations, with citation for comparison to human ES cells.

claim: Some differences to mouse iPSC cells include overall initial slower growth of cells.
source: Some differences to mouse iPSC cells include lack or little induction of Klf4, overall initial slower growth of cells, lower overall fold-expression increase in endogenous stem cell genes, and presence of autologously derived fibroblast cells for some of the avian species in the middle passages (Dai et al., unpublished date); the latter two traits are similar to some human ES cells (Draper et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Some differences to mouse iPSC cells include lower overall fold-expression increase in endogenous stem cell genes.
source: Some differences to mouse iPSC cells include lack or little induction of Klf4, overall initial slower growth of cells, lower overall fold-expression increase in endogenous stem cell genes, and presence of autologously derived fibroblast cells for some of the avian species in the middle passages (Dai et al., unpublished date); the latter two traits are similar to some human ES cells (Draper et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: In the quail and zebra finch iPSC-like cells Oct4 is 20–80-fold higher than in control fibroblasts, but lower than the 100–400-fold increase seen in the chicken and mouse cells.
source: For example, in the quail and zebra finch iPSC-like cells Oct4 is 20–80-fold higher than in control fibroblasts, but lower than the 100–400-fold increase seen in the chicken and mouse cells and yet not the 100–1000-fold increase typically seen in mouse cells (Soldner et al., 2009).
evidence: This is quantitative data from qRT-PCR, with citation for comparison.

claim: The fibroblast controls were from early embryos, which already had some Oct4 and Nanog expression (detected in PCR reactions by the 28th cycle).
source: We further note that our fibroblast controls were from early embryos, which already had some Oct4 and Nanog expression (detected in PCR reactions by the 28th cycle).
evidence: This is experimental observation about the control cells.

claim: Not only protocol differences exist between studies that affect expression levels, but species differences in induction levels for all four genes clearly exist.
source: Thus, we believe that not only protocol differences exist between studies that affect expression levels, but we clearly find species differences in induction levels for all four genes.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data and comparison to literature.

claim: Despite species differences, the lower levels of one or more of these genes was still sufficient to generate pluripotent cells.
source: Importantly, despite these species differences, the lower levels of one or more of these genes was still sufficient to generate pluripotent cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing pluripotency despite lower expression.

claim: It is not necessary for these genes to be induced 500–1000-fold in order for the cells to show some level of pluripotency in vitro or in vivo across species.
source: Thus, we conclude that is it is not necessary for these genes to be induced 500–1000-fold in order for the cells to show some level of pluripotency in vitro or in vivo across species.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: All species studied showed induced SSEA-1, but this gene is not induced in human iPSCs or ESCs.
source: All species we studied showed induced SSEA-1, but this gene is not induced in human iPSCs or ESCs (Takahashi et al., 2007), indicating that human cells might be different from other vertebrates or at a different stem cell state.
evidence: This is based on experimental data and comparison to published data with citation.

claim: Nanog was induced in all species except zebrafish.
source: Nanog was induced in all species except zebrafish.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: Nanog is the third master transcription factor in the stem cell regulatory system that promotes self renewal in the absence of LIF.
source: Nanog is the third master transcription factor in the stem cell regulatory system (Nichols et al., 2009; Silva et al., 2009) that promotes self renewal in the absence of LIF (Chambers and Tomlinson, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Recent studies suggest that Nanog may not be integrated in a pluripotency regulatory circuit in fish.
source: However, recent studies suggest that Nanog may not be integrated in a pluripotency regulatory circuit in fish (Camp et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Camp et al., 2009.

claim: The so-called fish Nanog homolog shows low sequence identity across much of the protein coding sequence with birds (32%) and mammals (31%).
source: We note, though, that the so-called fish Nanog homolog (NCBI Accession # NP_001091862) of these and many other studies show low sequence identity across much of the protein coding sequence with birds (32%) and mammals (31%).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis.

claim: It is possible that the fish Nanog homolog has not been really identified or is not present in the zebrafish genome.
source: In this regard, it is possible that the fish Nanog homolog has not been really identified or is not present in the zebrafish genome.
evidence: This is speculation based on the sequence analysis.

claim: The absence or very low induction of endogenous Klf4 in all of the non-mammalian species may either be due to an inability of the mammalian genes to re-program this gene, redundancy of the Klf family, or a lineage specific difference of mammals.
source: The absence or very low induction of endogenous Klf4 in all of the non-mammalian species may either be due to an inability of the mammalian genes to re-program this gene, redundancy of the Klf family (Jiang et al., 2008), or a lineage specific difference of mammals.
evidence: This is speculation about possible explanations, with citation for Klf family redundancy.

claim: The lineage specific difference hypothesis for Klf4 is supported by the low expression of Klf4 in chicken ESCs relative to control fibroblasts.
source: The later hypothesis is supported by the low expression of Klf4 in chicken ESCs relative to control fibroblasts.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: Induction of endogenous Klf4 has so far been found in several mammalian species, such as pig, mouse, and rats.
source: Induction of endogenous Klf4 has so far been found in several mammalian species, such as pig, mouse, and rats (Roberts et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Roberts et al., 2009.

claim: Klf4 preferentially regulates genes involved in cell adhesion, either activating or inhibiting adhesion, and cell adhesion can inhibit proliferation.
source: It has been shown that Klf4 preferentially regulates genes involved in cell adhesion, either activating or inhibiting adhesion, and that cell adhesion can inhibit proliferation (Swamynathan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Swamynathan et al., 2008.

claim: This function of Klf4 is consistent with findings that relative to mice, the non-mammalian iPSC-like cells are more adhesive to each other, which is known to slow proliferation even in mouse iPSCs.
source: This function is consistent with our findings that relative to mice, the non-mammalian iPSC-like cells are more adhesive to each other, which is known to slow proliferation even in mouse iPSCs (Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference connecting experimental observations to known function, with citation.

claim: The induced expression of endogenous Oct4, Sox2, (and partially of c-myc) homologs in all species and their continued expression when the mouse transgenes became silenced suggests that these genes may be playing more conserved inductive roles.
source: The induced expression of endogenous Oct4, Sox2, (and partially of c-myc) homologs in all species and their continued expression when the mouse transgenes became silenced suggests that these genes may be playing more conserved inductive roles.
evidence: This is an inference from the qRT-PCR data.

claim: Oct-4 and Sox-2, along with Nanog, are known as master transcription factors for the pluripotent stem cell state in mammalian cells.
source: Oct-4 and Sox-2, along with Nanog, are known as master transcription factors for the pluripotent stem cell state in mammalian cells (Chan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Chan et al., 2011.

claim: Oct4 and Sox2 can dimerize and when bound to DNA motifs of their target genes, they activate gene regulatory networks involved in both self-renewal and pluripotency.
source: Oct4 and Sox2 can dimerize and when bound to DNA motifs of their target genes, they activate gene regulatory networks involved in both self-renewal and pluripotency (Remenyi et al., 2003; Shi and Jin, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Sox2 alone has been shown to play various roles in different tissue types or cell states.
source: Sox2 alone has been shown to play various roles in different tissue types or cell states (Tomioka et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Tomioka et al., 2002.

claim: Oct-4 has been deemed the most important of these master factors in the mammalian stem cell regulatory system.
source: Oct-4 has been deemed the most important of these master factors in the mammalian stem cell regulatory system (Sterneckert et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Sterneckert et al., 2011.

claim: c-myc is known to induce proliferation, by repressing growth arresting genes.
source: Although not a master factor, c-myc is known to induce proliferation, by repressing growth arresting genes (Gartel and Shchors, 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Gartel and Shchors, 2003.

claim: c-myc is a key contributor in inducing the self-renewal state of the cell.
source: This makes it a key contributor in inducing the self-renewal state of the cell.
evidence: This is an inference from the known function of c-myc.

claim: Other factors that are less oncogenic have been shown to be suitable substitutes for c-myc, such as Gliss1.
source: Recently, other factors that are less oncogenic have been shown to be suitable substitutes for c-myc, such as Gliss1 (Maekawa et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Maekawa et al., 2011.

claim: A recent study showed that an intermediate state of stem cell induction can exist, by using just a few of the transcription factors.
source: A recent study also showed that an intermediate state of stem cell induction can exist, by using just a few of the transcription factors (Lin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lin et al., 2011.

claim: The cells from Lin et al. study did not successfully achieve pluripotency in vivo, different from the iPSC-like cells in this study.
source: Different from our iPSC-like cells they did not successfully achieve pluripotency in vivo.
evidence: This is a comparison to published work, with the current study's data showing in vivo pluripotency.

claim: The iPSC-like cells appear to be further along in the programming stage than the cells from Lin et al. study.
source: Thus, our cells appear to, at least, be further along in the programming stage than these cells.
evidence: This is an inference from comparison to published work.

claim: There are at least 7–8 stem cell marker genes up-regulated and three lineage specific germ layer genes down-regulated in the induced cells across species, relative to the embryonic fibroblasts.
source: All together, we show that there are at least 7–8 stem cell marker genes up-regulated and three lineage specific germ layer genes down-regulated in the induced cells across species, relative to the embryonic fibroblasts.
evidence: This is a summary of the qRT-PCR data.

claim: The results suggest that enough of a gene regulatory network was induced for the vertebrate cells to maintain a stem cell-like state in the absence of continued exogenous mouse transgene intervention.
source: While we have not performed full-scale transcriptome analysis or DNA methylation studies, the results suggest that enough of a gene regulatory network was induced for the vertebrate cells to maintain a stem cell-like state in the absence of continued exogenous mouse transgene intervention (Maherali and Hochedlinger, 2008), to become stably proliferative in optimal media conditions for the avian cells, and to become pluripotent in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data, with citation for context.

claim: The results suggest that enough of a gene regulatory network was induced for the avian cells to become stably proliferative in optimal media conditions.
source: While we have not performed full-scale transcriptome analysis or DNA methylation studies, the results suggest that enough of a gene regulatory network was induced for the vertebrate cells to maintain a stem cell-like state in the absence of continued exogenous mouse transgene intervention (Maherali and Hochedlinger, 2008), to become stably proliferative in optimal media conditions for the avian cells, and to become pluripotent in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference from the proliferation data.

claim: The results suggest that enough of a gene regulatory network was induced for the vertebrate cells to become pluripotent in vivo.
source: While we have not performed full-scale transcriptome analysis or DNA methylation studies, the results suggest that enough of a gene regulatory network was induced for the vertebrate cells to maintain a stem cell-like state in the absence of continued exogenous mouse transgene intervention (Maherali and Hochedlinger, 2008), to become stably proliferative in optimal media conditions for the avian cells, and to become pluripotent in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference from the in vivo pluripotency data.

claim: The induction of stem cell characteristics was less prominent in Drosophila than in the vertebrates.
source: First, the induction of stem cell characteristics was less prominent than in the vertebrates.
evidence: This is a comparative observation from the experimental data.

claim: When embryoid bodies were generated from Drosophila cells, they did so at a much lower rate than with the vertebrate cells.
source: When embryoid bodies were generated, they did so at a much lower rate with Drosophila cells than with the vertebrate cells.
evidence: This is quantitative observation from the experiments.

claim: Putative endogenous homolog expression did not occur in two of the genes for the S2 cells and in another three for the BG2 cells.
source: Putative endogenous homolog expression did not occur in two of the genes for the S2 cells and in another three for the BG2 cells.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: Proliferation was enhanced in transformed Drosophila cells, but the starting S2 cells were already relatively proliferative.
source: Second, proliferation was enhanced, but the starting S2 cells were already relatively proliferative.
evidence: This is based on MTT assay data and knowledge about S2 cells.

claim: S2 cells are partially differentiated, aneuploid, renewable cells.
source: This difference might be because S2 cells are partially differentiated, aneuploid, renewable cells (Moutinho-Pereira et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about S2 cells supported by citation.

claim: One interpretation is that the S2 cells underwent transdifferentiation as a result of the presence of mammalian stem cell genes, but for a stem cell state.
source: One interpretation of these findings is that the S2 cells underwent transdifferentiation as a result of the presence of mammalian stem cell genes, but for a stem cell state; that is switching from one highly proliferative state to another.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the Drosophila data.

claim: The findings suggest that the closer the relationship to mammals, the more reprogrammed characteristics the cells showed.
source: Altogether, the findings suggest that the closer the relationship to mammals, the more reprogrammed characteristics the cells showed.
evidence: This is an inference from comparing data across species.

claim: Substituted gene function among vertebrates has been demonstrated previously.
source: Substituted gene function among vertebrates (Enard et al., 2009) and between vertebrates and invertebrates (Lavial et al., 2007) has been demonstrated previously, but we are not aware of a systematic set of genes doing so.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Enard et al., 2009 and Lavial et al., 2007.

claim: Substituted gene function between vertebrates and invertebrates has been demonstrated previously.
source: Substituted gene function among vertebrates (Enard et al., 2009) and between vertebrates and invertebrates (Lavial et al., 2007) has been demonstrated previously, but we are not aware of a systematic set of genes doing so.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lavial et al., 2007.

claim: It is possible that a stem cell gene regulatory network and the stem cells themselves share more conserved molecular similarities than differentiated divergent cells.
source: It is possible that a stem cell gene regulatory network and the stem cells themselves share more conserved molecular similarities than differentiated divergent cells.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings.

claim: Oct4 has been shown to regulate some of the same genes, including Sox2, in mammals and fish.
source: This idea is supported by the fact that Oct4 has been shown to regulate some of the same genes, including Sox2, in mammals and fish (Onichtchouk et al., 2010), and embryonic cells and the three germ layers are more similar to each other in distantly related organisms than their adult cells, which are more divergent (Parikh et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Onichtchouk et al., 2010.

claim: Embryonic cells and the three germ layers are more similar to each other in distantly related organisms than their adult cells, which are more divergent.
source: This idea is supported by the fact that Oct4 has been shown to regulate some of the same genes, including Sox2, in mammals and fish (Onichtchouk et al., 2010), and embryonic cells and the three germ layers are more similar to each other in distantly related organisms than their adult cells, which are more divergent (Parikh et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Parikh et al., 2010.

claim: The iPSC features were maintained in the vertebrate cells even after the mouse transgenes were suppressed.
source: This is further supported by the finding that the iPSC features were maintained in the vertebrate cells even after the mouse transgenes were suppressed.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing continued expression of endogenous genes and stem cell features after transgene silencing.

claim: The findings suggest that stem cells could represent a primordial animal cell state conserved across the animal kingdom.
source: As such, our findings suggest that stem cells could represent a primordial animal cell state conserved across the animal kingdom.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings.

claim: The generation of in vivo incorporating stem cells for non-mammalian species should help advance studies of these experimental model systems.
source: In summary, the generation of in vivo incorporating stem cells for non-mammalian species should help advance studies of these experimental model systems.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications.

claim: These cells can be used as tools to study differentiation, evolution, and disease across a wide range of species, including cancer.
source: These cells can be used as tools to study differentiation, evolution, and disease across a wide range of species, including cancer (Takashima et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about applications, with citation for cancer studies.

claim: The induced cells might serve as a platform to study cellular evolution at the molecular level.
source: The induced cells might serve as a platform to study cellular evolution at the molecular level.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications.
